newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end week steady, seen moving higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end week steady, seen moving higher.

text.p: Swiss shares ended little changed on Friday in quiet pre-weekend trade as the positive effect of a firmer dollar was offset by some profit taking.
"It was very quiet and nobody wanted to take positions ahead of the weekend," one dealer said.
The market was seen moving higher again next week due to low Swiss interest rates and the dollar's solid performance.
"I think we will see a level of 6,000 SMI points again," one trader noted, adding there was no real alternative to shares.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 2.2 points, or 0.04 percent, at 5,847.0 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) moved in the opposite direction, adding 3.68 points to 3,712.49.
Bourse volume reached 2.5 billion Swiss francs.
Dealers said several dollar-sensitive stocks such as cement company Holderbank and watchmaker SMH were supported by the dollar's surge above 1.50 Swiss francs.
SMH bearer shares jumped 29 francs, or more than three percent, to 891.
Part of the rise could be due to the fact that the stock has been lagging the market for some time, dealers said.
Banks were mixed. Most-active UBS bearers fell two francs to 1,689, while CS Group and SBC saw gains.
Among insurers, Winterthur, which saw massive gains this year due to merger speculation, stood aout with an advanced of 38 francs to 1,474.

Novartis registered shares continued Thursday's fall, dropping 21 francs to 2,379. Thursday's half-year sales figures were in line with forecasts but this disappointed some investors who had speculated on more and put pressure on the share, one dealer said.
Roche certificates fell back from intra-day highs at 14,950 to end unchanged at 14,750.
Specialty chemicals firm Clariant continued to profit from Wednesday's favourable half-year sales figures, surging 22 francs to 1,100.
Swiss Life, which on Thursday jumped nine percent, added 15 francs to 815.
